<!-- validation-comment-start --><body>Hello there! From the DISABLED prefix in this issue title, it looks like you are attempting to disable a test in PyTorch CI. The information I have parsed is below:

* Test name: `test_fn_gradgrad_cholesky_solve_cuda_complex128 (__main__.TestBwdGradientsCUDA)`
* Platforms for which to skip the test: rocm
* Disabled by `pytorch-bot[bot]`

Within ~15 minutes, `test_fn_gradgrad_cholesky_solve_cuda_complex128 (__main__.TestBwdGradientsCUDA)` will be disabled in PyTorch CI for these platforms: rocm. Please verify that your test name looks correct, e.g., `test_cuda_assert_async (__main__.TestCuda)`.

To modify the platforms list, please include a line in the issue body, like below. The default action will disable the test for all platforms if no platforms list is specified. 
```
Platforms: case-insensitive, list, of, platforms
```
We currently support the following platforms: asan, dynamo, inductor, linux, mac, macos, rocm, slow, win, windows, xpu.


### How to re-enable a test
To re-enable the test globally, close the issue. To re-enable a test for only a subset of platforms, remove the platforms from the list in the issue body. This may take some time to propagate. To re-enable a test only for a PR, put `Fixes #164193` in the PR body and rerun the test jobs. Note that if a test is flaky, it maybe be difficult to tell if the test is still flaky on the PR.
</body><!-- validation-comment-end -->
